title: Lab protocol for investigating impacts of climate change on frogs
author: Saeed, Rais, et al.

steps.title: Collect wild specimens
steps.instruction: Capture adult male and female frogs from streams and springs (e.g., Murree, District Rawalpindi, Punjab and Ayubia National Park, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) between February 2018 and October 2019, and collect larvae using dip nets, selecting individuals at the desired Gosner stage (e.g., stage 25) for experiments.

substeps.instruction: Capture adult frogs of both sexes from natural habitats.
Collect larvae with dip nets and retain those at the target Gosner stage.

steps.title: Select viable temperature gradient
steps.instruction: Perform a preliminary trial to identify temperatures that do not cause 100 % mortality.

substeps.instruction: Place five adult males, five adult females, and 25 tadpoles (Gosner stage 25) of each species in plastic buckets (45 × 35 × 48 cm) for 24 h at each test temperature: 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 30, 32 °C.
Record mortality after 24 h; exclude temperatures with 100 % mortality (30 °C and 32 °C for Allopaa hazarensis; 28 °C, 30 °C and 32 °C for Nanorana vicina).
Note ambient seasonal water temperatures for reference: 14 °C (March‑April), 23 °C (May‑June), 22 °C (July‑August), 11 °C (September‑October).

steps.title: Set up adult temperature exposure
steps.instruction: Expose the experimental adult frogs to the selected temperature range.

substeps.instruction: Allocate 200 adult frogs (10 males + 10 females per temperature per species) to the chosen temperatures; keep 160 frogs (40 males + 40 females per species) as controls at ambient temperature.
Place each temperature group in plastic buckets (45 × 35 × 48 cm) at a field station near the habitat and expose for 24 h at the assigned temperature.

steps.title: Prepare frogs for hormone sampling
steps.instruction: Condition, measure, sex, and mark each adult frog before blood collection.

substeps.instruction: After temperature exposure, keep each frog in a clean plastic bucket for an additional 24 h.
Measure snout‑vent length with a digital vernier caliper (or INSIZE Electronic Calipers series 1112, 0.01 mm) and body mass with a balance (0.01 g).
Determine sex by secondary sexual characters: females have a soft belly and lack a nuptial pad on the thumb; males possess a nuptial pad.
Mark each individual by toe‑clipping or PIT‑tagging.
Release the marked frog back into its original habitat.
Perform cardiac puncture using a 30‑gauge insulin syringe (1 mL/cc) to draw blood.
Transfer the blood into K3EDTA (EDTA) tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes for 30 minutes at 3000 rpm to separate plasma.
Store the plasma on ice or at –20 °C until ELISA testing.

steps.title: Quantify estradiol and testosterone by ELISA
steps.instruction: Measure sex hormone concentrations in plasma using commercial ELISA kits.

substeps.instruction: Prepare reagents and standards according to the Fish Estradiol (E2) ELISA kit (Catalogue SL0033FI) and Fish Testosterone ELISA kit (Catalogue SL0032FI) protocols.
Add plasma samples and standards to the ELISA plates, follow incubation, washing, and detection steps as described in the kits.
Read absorbance at the specified wavelength and calculate hormone concentrations using the standard curves.

steps.title: Set up larval rearing aquaria
steps.instruction: Prepare temperature‑controlled aquaria for tadpole growth experiments.

substeps.instruction: Fill glass aquaria (38 × 30 × 42 cm) with 15 L of tap water.
Regulate water temperature with a temperature controller set to 16–34 °C ± 0.5 °C.
Install an aerator with a stone for air circulation and a filter, operating the filter 4 hours per day.
Divide larvae of each species into five batches (100 larvae per batch, 25 larvae per replication) and place them into the prepared aquaria.

steps.title: Maintain larvae and record growth
steps.instruction: Conduct the larval experiment, monitoring development, morphology, and survival.

substeps.instruction: Feed larvae twice daily with boiled spinach/vegetable and supplement with fish meal.
Monitor and record water temperature daily.
Record developmental stage (Gosner stages 25–46) weekly.

Measure morphometric parameters weekly: total length, snout‑vent length (SVL), tail length, maximum body width, maximum tail length, body height, maximum tail height, maximum total height, and body mass.
Count dead tadpoles each day to calculate mortality rates.
Examine larvae for gross morphological deformities such as edema (abdominal swelling) and tail kink (twist/curve), following the criteria of Wolf et al. 1969 and Chinathamby et al.

steps.title: Conclude larval experiment
steps.instruction: Terminate the growth trial and compile data.

substeps.instruction: Continue the experiment for 21 weeks for Allopaa hazarensis and 24 weeks for Nanorana vicina.
At the end of the trial, gather all growth, survival, and deformity data for statistical analysis.
